name: Black & Veatch
legalName: Black & Veatch (100% employee-owned via ESOP since 2015; employee-owned corporation since 1999)
founded: 1915 (Ernest Bateman Black & Nathan Thomas Veatch, Kansas City)
employees: ~13,000 (2025); among the largest 100% employee-owned US companies (top-10, rank drifting upward)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Black & Veatch is the grid-and-water engineer betting its AI-era franchise on client-owned substations — building hyperscalers' and colocation operators' own transmission-connected substations (a six-site global program for a leading colocation company; two 300 MW units for a confidential US hyperscale campus, the first completed September 2025) to cut interconnection timelines 'by one-half or more' versus waiting 5+ years for utility build-out. The ~13,000-person, 100% ESOP-owned Overland Park firm posted record ~$5.0-5.1B 2025 revenue (from $4.3B in 2022) and holds a nearly unique ENR breadth: #6 Power AND #8 Water simultaneously, plus #1 in Hydrogen (EPC of the ACES Delta green-hydrogen hub: 220 MW of electrolyzers, 100 t/day, two salt caverns), #1 in O&M, and a seat in one of the first US SMR design-build contracts (the equal Aecon-Kiewit-B&V 'Cascade Nuclear Partners' JV for the first four X-energy Xe-100s at Energy Northwest's Amazon-backed facility). Two strategic retreats mark the modern shape: exit from new coal (2020) and the $150M sale of its public-carrier wireless business to Dycom (August 2024, ~$1B backlog transferred). Watch items: no named behind-the-meter AI-campus gas plant (rivals Kiewit, B&W, and Gemma hold those awards — B&V plays owner's engineer and substations instead); the Boldt wind-farm litigation turned adverse (a $1 nominal award on B&V's $29.4M claim, affirmed July 2026, with a new trial ordered on Boldt's wrongful-termination claim); and two restructurings in 22 months with unconfirmed January 2026 layoff reports.
ecosystemRole: The interconnection specialist of the AI buildout: engineer-builder of the client-owned substations, grid infrastructure, cooling water systems, hydrogen hubs, and first SMRs that connect gigawatt campuses to power — selling speed around the utility queue rather than competing for the buildings themselves.

productsAndServices.name: Data Centers & Client-Owned Substations
productsAndServices.description: End-to-end 'one partner' model for hyperscale, colocation, and neocloud data centers — site selection, permitting, design, procurement, construction, utility interconnection, commissioning, O&M — housed in the Technology, Industrial & Governments sector. The signature product is the client-owned substation: B&V builds the data-center operator's own transmission-connected substation, halving (or better) the interconnection timeline versus utility build-out, with 24/7 remote monitoring layered on.
highlights: Six-site global substation program for a 'leading global colocation company' — B&V sizes modern hyperscale campuses at 400 MW-2 GW

Two 300 MW substations for a confidential US hyperscale developer (progressive design-build, open-to-closed-book): first completed September 2025; circuit breakers procured in 48-65 weeks vs ~85-week market lead times
LATAM hyperscale campus full detailed design (IFC packages, LEED Gold); commissioning of a 'world's first zero-water-consumption data center' (client undisclosed)

2025 Electric Report: 53% of utilities cite limited available power as the top data-center obstacle; data centers build in ~18 months vs ~6 years for grid infrastructure — the gap B&V's product monetizes
productsAndServices.positioning: The picks-and-shovels grid specialist of the DC boom — not competing with shell GCs (HITT, Holder, Turner) but selling the interconnection speed every campus needs; rival Burns & McDonnell sells a similar utility-side thesis from across town
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Progressive design-build and EPC contracts directly with data-center operators, plus utility frameworks
productsAndServices.roadmap: Scaling the client-owned substation model as interconnection queues lengthen

productsAndServices.name: Power Generation & Hydrogen
productsAndServices.description: A century-old power franchise now spanning hydrogen-capable gas, LNG-to-power, and utility-scale renewables: owner's engineer on IPP Renewed (Intermountain Power, Utah — the 840 MW hydrogen-capable combined cycle that replaced 1,800 MW of coal, entered commercial operation Jul-Oct 2025), topline EPC of the Philippines' first LNG-to-power project (1,275 MW H-class, commissioned early 2025), and EPC of ACES Delta — 'the world's first and largest industrial green hydrogen hub' (220 MW electrolyzers, 100 metric tons H2/day, two salt caverns) feeding IPP Renewed next door. ENR #1 Hydrogen, #2 Co-Generation, #3 Solar, #1 O&M (2026).
highlights: IPP Renewed: system studies, technology selection, HVDC converter stations, and conversion of two 900 MW coal generators to synchronous condensers (construction EPC was Kiewit's TIC with Mitsubishi Power — B&V is Owner's Engineer, a commonly misattributed role)
ACES Delta: green hydrogen at industrial-first scale, guaranteed 30% H2 blend at the plant's startup rising to 100% by 2045
Exited new coal work entirely in 2020; utility-scale solar EPC includes Avangrid's largest solar project, built partly to serve Texas data-center demand
productsAndServices.positioning: Deep gas/hydrogen engineering with lighter hard-dollar mega-EPC exposure than Bechtel/Kiewit — notably, no named behind-the-meter AI-campus gas plant yet (that niche is held by Kiewit, B&W, and Gemma); B&V's power monetization of AI runs through substations, OE roles, and design
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC, owner's-engineer, and progressive design-build contracts
productsAndServices.roadmap: Hydrogen-hub replication; gas fleet advisory as AI load drives new CCGT demand

productsAndServices.name: Power Delivery (Transmission, Distribution & Grid)
productsAndServices.description: 75+ years of grid experience, a 1,400+ person grid workforce, and 2,600+ active grid projects across transmission, distribution, substations, grid modernization, and storage integration — with self-perform field capability added by the May 2023 acquisition of Bird Electric (~600 T&D/electrical staff). Named work includes AEP substation EPC in West Texas and Georgia Power grid-investment support.
highlights: The delivery muscle behind the client-owned substation product
Duke Energy named B&V its 2026 Corporate Responsibility Supplier of the Year, citing BESS, substations, distribution, solar, and telecom work
Construction subsidiaries: B&V Construction (1991), Overland Contracting (1996), Bird Electric (2023); record 24.5M craft hours in 2023
productsAndServices.positioning: Smaller than Quanta/MasTec in field T&D but pairs construction with top-6 power design authority — the engineer-builder hybrid in the grid lane
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility EPC and framework agreements; direct DC-operator contracts

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear / SMR (Cascade JV)
productsAndServices.description: An equal-share member of 'Cascade Nuclear Partners' — the Aecon + Kiewit Nuclear Solutions + Black & Veatch JV selected by Energy Northwest (October 2025) under a progressive design-build model to plan, design, and construct the first 4 of 12 X-energy Xe-100 SMRs (320 MW initial phase) at the Cascade Advanced Energy Facility in Richland, WA — the Amazon-backed deployment adjacent to Columbia Generating Station.
highlights: One of the first US SMR design-build contracts — and B&V's seat came by teaming with Kiewit rather than bidding against it
Broader nuclear services and SMR advisory/owner's-engineering practice
productsAndServices.positioning: Early execution position in the hyperscaler-underwritten SMR class, at JV scale that fits its balance sheet
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Progressive design-build JV with a public power agency
productsAndServices.roadmap: First-four-unit execution; option scope to 12 units

productsAndServices.name: Water & Connectivity (legacy franchises)
productsAndServices.description: One of America's great water engineers (ENR #8 Top Water Design Firms): drinking water, wastewater, reuse ('One Water'), desalination, conveyance, and industrial/data-center water including cooling and zero-water designs (Pure Water Soquel groundwater replenishment is a named flagship). The telecom franchise was deliberately shrunk: the public-carrier wireless business sold to Dycom for $150M (August 2024, ~$1B backlog transferred); what remains focuses on private networks and grid communications — including the March 2025 arrangement making B&V exclusive sales agent for Grain Management's T-Mobile 800 MHz spectrum for critical utility communications.
highlights: Simultaneous top-10 ENR standing in Power and Water is nearly unique among US engineers
Data-center water is a genuine AI adjacency: cooling design and zero-water commissioning credentials
Principal engineering/construction partner on one of the world's largest contiguous EV-charging buildouts (program attribution low confidence)
productsAndServices.positioning: Water breadth differentiates against power-only rivals; the wireless exit traded scale for focus
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Municipal procurement, industrial contracts, spectrum agency arrangement
productsAndServices.roadmap: Data-center water/cooling demand; utility private-network buildout

recentDevelopments.headline: Duke Energy names Black & Veatch its 2026 Corporate Responsibility Supplier of the Year, citing BESS, substation, distribution, solar, and telecom work
recentDevelopments.read: Utility-relationship depth is the distribution channel for the whole AI-era thesis — awards like this are the trust the client-owned-substation product rides on.

recentDevelopments.headline: Seventh Circuit affirms the $1 nominal-damages verdict on B&V's ~$29.4M Boldt wind-farm counterclaim — and orders a new trial on Boldt's wrongful-termination claim
recentDevelopments.read: The dispute has inverted: B&V's own recovery is dead, and exposure now runs against it. Also a sector-wide precedent on written-notice-of-delay provisions in EPC subcontracts.
recentDevelopments.source: CA7 No. 25-2070 via Justia; National Law Review, 2026-07-16

recentDevelopments.headline: Annual growth release confirms the three-sector structure (Fuels & Natural Resources; Technology, Industrial & Governments; Power Providers) plus Infrastructure Advisory; CEO Azar frames AI-driven power demand as the core growth driver
recentDevelopments.read: The second reorganization in 22 months — the org chart now explicitly mirrors the AI-infrastructure demand map. No revenue or backlog figures were disclosed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Anonymous employee reports describe no-notice January 2026 layoffs allegedly timed ahead of the March bonus-eligibility date (no mainstream press confirmation — low confidence)
recentDevelopments.read: Employee-sentiment signal only — but paired with two restructurings in 22 months, it suggests integration friction behind the record top line.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2025 Electric Report: 53% of surveyed utilities cite limited available power as the top obstacle to connecting data centers; only 19% are confident in their load forecasts
recentDevelopments.read: B&V's own market research doubles as product marketing — the 18-month data center vs 6-year grid mismatch is precisely what its client-owned substations arbitrage.
recentDevelopments.source: B&V 2025 Electric Report; American Public Power Association coverage

recentDevelopments.headline: Energy Northwest selects Cascade Nuclear Partners — an equal Aecon / Kiewit Nuclear Solutions / Black & Veatch JV — as progressive design-builder for the first 4 of 12 X-energy Xe-100 SMRs (up to 320 MW) at Richland, WA
recentDevelopments.read: One of the first US SMR design-build seats, on the Amazon-backed program — and B&V got there by teaming with Kiewit rather than fighting it.
recentDevelopments.source: Aecon/GlobeNewswire, 2025-10-23; World Nuclear News; Energy Northwest

recentDevelopments.headline: Completes the first of two 300 MW client-owned substations for a confidential US hyperscale campus; the second began construction at year-end — with circuit breakers procured in 48-65 weeks against ~85-week market lead times
recentDevelopments.read: The signature product delivered at speed: progressive design-build, early procurement of long-lead grid gear, and a claimed 3 months cut from schedule.

recentDevelopments.headline: IPP Renewed's 840 MW hydrogen-capable combined cycle enters commercial operation (Jul-Oct 2025) with B&V as Owner's Engineer; the two 900 MW coal units retire, converted to synchronous condensers
recentDevelopments.read: The flagship coal-to-hydrogen-capable-gas conversion in US power — B&V held the engineering brain role while Kiewit's TIC built it, a division of labor that captures B&V's whole positioning.

recentDevelopments.headline: Named exclusive sales agent and industry partner for Grain Management's T-Mobile 800 MHz spectrum, marketed for critical utility and private-network communications
recentDevelopments.read: The post-Dycom telecom strategy in miniature: out of public-carrier wireless construction, into utility-grade private networks where its grid relationships rule.

recentDevelopments.headline: The Philippines' first LNG-to-power project — 1,275 MW net H-class combined cycle plus substation — is commissioned with B&V as topline EPC
recentDevelopments.read: Proof the full-EPC muscle still exists at gigawatt scale internationally, even as US mega-EPC stays selective.

recentDevelopments.headline: A jury awards B&V just $1 on its $29.4M excess-completion-cost claim against Boldt (Cardinal Point 150 MW wind farm)
recentDevelopments.read: ENR called it a 'surprise' — jurors did not credit B&V's cost evidence, the beginning of the litigation's adverse turn.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sells its public-carrier wireless telecom infrastructure business to Dycom for $150M cash — ~$250-275M of annual revenue and ~$1B of backlog transferred
recentDevelopments.read: A decisive franchise exit: trading a shrinking-margin carrier business for focus on power, water, and data-center infrastructure. Subcontractors reportedly learned of the sale late — a minor partner-relations blemish.
recentDevelopments.source: Dycom IR release, 2024-08-21; Construction Dive; RCR Wireless

recentDevelopments.headline: Restructures into five client-facing areas with explicit callouts to AI computing, gigafactories, and data centers; workforce grows 17% to over 12,000 with 'historic levels of project backlog'
recentDevelopments.read: The first of the two reorganizations — the moment the firm formally re-aimed itself at the AI-infrastructure demand set.

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess the client-owned substation is Black & Veatch's defining AI-era product: by building the data-center operator's own transmission-connected substation, it converts the industry's central mismatch (campuses built in ~18 months vs ~6-year grid timelines) into a repeatable, high-urgency offering — six sites for one colocation client, 300 MW units for a hyperscaler, early-procured breakers beating market lead times by ~20-37 weeks. It monetizes the queue without owning generation risk.

2. (High confidence) We assess B&V is deliberately positioned as engineer-brain rather than mega-EPC-balance-sheet in the AI power race: Owner's Engineer on IPP Renewed (Kiewit built it), design-builder in a three-way SMR JV (with Kiewit), substations rather than shells — lower risk and lower headline share than Bechtel/Kiewit, matched to a ~$5B ESOP balance sheet. The absence of a named behind-the-meter AI-campus gas award (a niche Kiewit, B&W, and Gemma hold) is the strategy's cost, not an accident.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess the simultaneous top-10 Power and Water design standing — nearly unique in the industry — is quietly compounding in the AI cycle: cooling-water design, zero-water commissioning, and reuse engineering are becoming procurement criteria as water politics tighten around data centers, and no power-first rival carries B&V's water bench.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the portfolio pruning (new coal exited 2020; public-carrier wireless sold 2024 with ~$1B of backlog) shows disciplined franchise management: both exits shed structurally deteriorating businesses ahead of the pain and concentrated capital on grid, generation transition, hydrogen (#1 ENR), and data centers. The Grain/T-Mobile spectrum agency role is the telecom remnant re-aimed at utilities.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess execution and organizational strain as the live internal risk: a $1 verdict on a $29.4M claim (jurors rejecting its cost evidence) with a wrongful-termination retrial now running against it, two restructurings in 22 months, and unconfirmed no-notice layoff reports — none existential, but together a pattern that ESOP cultures absorb poorly and competitors exploit in recruiting.

6. (Low confidence) We assess the Cascade SMR JV could become the franchise-defining position of the 2030s if the Xe-100 program executes — an equal seat in one of the first US SMR design-build contracts, on an Amazon-backed program, with option scope to 12 units. Treat as high-value optionality: first-of-a-kind nuclear schedules routinely slip, and JV economics are undisclosed.

relationships.note: Equal partners in Cascade Nuclear Partners (with Aecon) — first 4 of 12 X-energy Xe-100 SMRs at Energy Northwest — and complementary roles on IPP Renewed (B&V engineered, Kiewit built).
relationships.context: Energy Northwest selected the Aecon / Kiewit Nuclear Solutions / Black & Veatch JV in October 2025 as progressive design-builder for up to 320 MW of Xe-100 SMRs at Richland, WA — one of the first US SMR design-build seats, on the Amazon-backed program. On IPP Renewed's 840 MW hydrogen-capable combined cycle, B&V held the Owner's Engineer role while Kiewit built — the engineer-brain vs builder division of labor that defines B&V's positioning. They remain rivals elsewhere: Kiewit holds the behind-the-meter AI-campus gas awards B&V lacks.

relationships.note: Indirect: the Cascade SMR JV serves Energy Northwest's Amazon-backed Xe-100 deployment — no direct B&V–Amazon contract is documented.
relationships.context: The dossier rates the Cascade seat as potentially franchise-defining for the 2030s if the Xe-100 program executes, with option scope to 12 units on a program Amazon backs.

decisionMakers.name: Mario Azar
decisionMakers.title: Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
background: Eighth leader in the company's 110-year history; CEO since 2022, having joined in 2018 as President of the global Power business (board member 2021)
Prior: multiple global roles at Siemens (including global CEO of its Oil & Gas and Marine business) and Westinghouse (started as a manufacturing quality engineer)
BS electrical engineering, UNC Charlotte; boards include the US Energy Association and Kansas City civic organizations
Frames AI-driven power demand as the firm's core growth driver in its 2026 strategy release
